title: The Hollow Crown
premise: Isandro Yarrow has spent seven years as the last gatekeeper of the Hollow Door, selling harmless charms in a city where magic is punishable by death, hiding the truth that the seal she tends is failing. When a mute child arrives speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the Old Blood, Isandro realizes the child is a living key—and that the king's witch-hunters have followed her. Torn between loyalty to the city that sheltered her and the truth that the ancient war never ended but only paused, Isandro must choose: reseal the door with her own life, or open it and let the old powers return. In the end, she does neither—she passes the key to the child, sacrifices her magic to buy the city one honest generation, and walks into the long winter knowing some crowns are hollow because they were never meant to be worn.
about_author: W. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed collections in northern university libraries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about doors, debts, and the people paid to keep both shut.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On the eve of the first snow, Isandro sells a luck-knot to a frightened fishwife, hides her real work beneath floorboards, and performs her nightly ritual at the Hollow Door. The beat is weary routine masking dread—the reader feels seven years of held breath.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A barefoot girl appears at Isandro's shop speaking a language that makes the wards hum, clutching a crown-shaped iron token. The emotional beat is terror curdling into recognition: the child's words are the same ones carved above the Door.

chapters.title: What the Seal Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with flashback. Isandro tests the girl, Vess, and learns the seal responds to her blood. Flashback reveals how Isandro inherited the gatekeeper's oath from her dying mentor. The beat is reluctant inheritance becoming unbearable responsibility.

chapters.title: The Ashen Order
chapters.summary: Captain Rellane's POV. Introduces the king's witch-hunter, who arrives in Greyhollow hunting rumors of 'living script.' Rellane is not a monster—she lost family to the last war. The beat is chilling sympathy: the antagonist believes she is saving everyone.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A neighbor Isandro loves, the tanner Odrik, notices Vess and asks dangerous questions. Isandro lies to him for the first time. The beat is love strained by secrecy—loyalty beginning to cost more than truth would.

chapters.title: The Language Under Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. Through the child's eyes we see flashes of what she fled: burning towers, a voice beneath ice calling her name. The beat is haunting innocence—Vess doesn't know she is a weapon; she only knows she was told to find the keeper.

chapters.title: Ash on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Rellane searches the shop district; Isandro hides Vess inside the Hollow Door's antechamber, breaking protocol. The beat is claustrophobic suspense ending in a terrible discovery: someone has already scratched counter-sigils into the outer stone.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Mark
chapters.summary: Rellane's POV. Rellane interrogates the district and realizes the sigils match records from her order's forbidden archive—meaning someone inside Greyhollow wants the Door open. The beat is shifting suspicion: the hunters may be hunted by their own ally.

chapters.title: Odrik's Choice
chapters.summary: Odrik's POV. Odrik discovers Isandro's hidden charms and must decide whether to report her. He burns his own ledger of debts instead and offers help. The beat is quiet heroism—ordinary loyalty outweighing survival instinct.

chapters.title: Beneath the Ice, a Voice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The seal cracks during a storm; Isandro hears the entity below speak her mentor's voice, offering bargains. She refuses, barely. The beat is temptation rendered intimate—the enemy knows exactly which face to wear.

chapters.title: The Archive of Burned Names
chapters.summary: Isandro and Odrik's alternating POV. They break into the Order's archive seeking the original terms of the seal and learn the war ended not in victory but in a hostage exchange: the Old Blood gave a child-key; the kingdoms gave up magic forever. The beat is revelation rewriting everything Isandro believed about her duty.

chapters.title: Half a Crown
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro confronts the truth: Vess is the hostage, returned because the other side broke faith—or claims it did. The iron token is half of the Hollow Crown; the other half is below. The beat is grief and fury at being the last link in a lie.

chapters.title: Rellane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rellane's POV. Rellane finds the archive disturbed and identifies Odrik, but hesitates when she reads the original treaty and recognizes her own grandmother's signature among those who surrendered the city's magic. The beat is the antagonist's faith fracturing.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The winter deepens unnaturally early; crops fail, and the city blames witches. Mobs form. The beat is societal dread—survival pressure making truth impossible to speak publicly.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro visits her mentor's grave and admits she cannot hold the seal alone through winter. She decides to seek the third option no one recorded: reforge the Crown whole so no side can wield it. The beat is resolve born from surrender.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Isandro, Vess, and Odrik enter the passages beneath the Door. Traps keyed to Old Blood nearly kill Vess; Isandro takes the wound meant for her. The beat is sacrificial love—duty and devotion finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: The Court Below
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. In the deep hall they meet the entity wearing Isandro's mentor's face and the frozen court of the Old Blood, who claim Vess was stolen, not surrendered. The beat is moral vertigo—both sides' histories cannot be true at once.

chapters.title: Two Halves, One Lie
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro learns the full truth: there was never a war to resume—the Old Blood died out long ago, and what remains below is grief given power, sustained by the hostage ritual. The Crown is hollow because it holds nothing but mourning. The beat is devastating clarity.

chapters.title: The Witch-Hunter's Blade
chapters.summary: Rellane's POV. Rellane descends after them, blade drawn, and finds not monsters but a starving child and a bleeding keeper. Ordered to kill, she instead cuts her own order's sigil from her coat. The beat is the antagonist's redemption through chosen treason.

chapters.title: Crowning the Grief
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. The entity demands its key back; Isandro joins the two halves of the Crown and offers it not to either side but to the mourning itself, letting the dead court finally end. The seal transforms rather than breaks. The beat is cathartic climax—truth spoken aloud at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: The Price of the Keeper
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The reforging consumes Isandro's magic; she survives but is ordinary now, her charms just knots and string. Vess chooses to stay with Odrik rather than return below. The beat is bittersweet loss—survival achieved, but paid for in identity.

chapters.title: Spring, Eventually
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Vess's POV, years later. The winter ends; Greyhollow slowly permits small magics again under new honest law. Vess, now apprentice keeper, opens the shop door to another strange child. The beat is hopeful continuity—some doors must stay open, tended by those who remember why.
